blockers.title: SIGCHLD is reset rather than required already default
blockers.evidence: Root previous_chld=signal.signal(SIGCHLD,SIG_DFL) and caller old_chld=signal.signal(SIGCHLD,SIG_DFL) mutate the disposition; neither first requires the prior disposition be default. Caller later restores the previous value. This contradicts the accepted already-default/no-reset/no-competing-waiter source contract and can accept startup after silently changing an unsupported ownership assumption.
blockers.bounded_correction: Before any owned construction require signal.getsignal(SIGCHLD)==SIG_DFL and refuse otherwise without resetting it. Preserve the default/no competing waiter assumption and pending installed-runtime/SA_NOCLDWAIT proof; do not infer it from a reset or restore an unsupported value during finalization.

blockers.title: ECHILD does not revoke numeric PID signal authority
blockers.evidence: Exact waitpid and stopped-handshake paths do not latch ChildProcessError/lost direct-child relationship. If waitpid raises ECHILD, the record can remain unreaped; generic error handling then reaches query own-PID SIGKILL or preCONT own-PID SIGKILL. A returned historical handle/PID is insufficient once the direct-child relationship is unavailable; that numeric PID may no longer be owned.
blockers.bounded_correction: Record a distinct lost/unknown direct-child relationship at the exact failing wait, preserve the exception and close all numeric PID/group signal authority for that handle. Signal only a positively retained unreaped relationship. Keep ESRCH from a kill distinct: it is not a reap or absence and must not skip a separately bounded explicit wait while direct ownership remains valid. No guessed cleanup/absence, default polling or replacement child.

blockers.title: A timely normal receipt deadline is necessarily rejected as future
blockers.evidence: caller_evidence calls clock_token on every clock value, including normal_until_ns. clock_token rejects integers greater than current monotonic_ns. A timely candidate must still be before normal_until_ns, so the deadline is necessarily future; waiting until it ceases to be future violates the same normal95 gate. The normal success path is therefore infeasible.
blockers.bounded_correction: Separate canonical positive-ASCII integer parsing from observed-timestamp<=now validation. Keep the latter for original start and actual observed entry/spawn/encoding/saved/hash timestamps; validate normal_until_ns by the exact min(originalStart+95s,callerEntry+100s) equation and all original ordering/boundary constraints. Do not remove observed-time validation or relax any deadline.

blockers.title: Final receipt write has no required postwrite finite identity join
blockers.evidence: The identity equality/candidate is calculated before final encoding/write. After write_full the owner checks budgets and time only. The accepted control-contract receipt_write_policy.owner_final explicitly requires postwrite identity checks as well; an admitted input/source/actual changed during final serialization/write need not be detected by the owner before raw0.
blockers.bounded_correction: After the complete receipt write recheck the same finite identity set within the original115 bound. Mismatch/error/late return must force raw refusal and preserve the prefinal receipt unchanged; no rewritten positive artifact or renewed deadline. Independent root full-return/status/census/identity observations remain additional requirements.
